say: For example, Funmi in Lagos paid a carpenter a deposit for a wardrobe. Weeks later, it has not arrived, and he has stopped replying clearly.

card.title: Funmi's wardrobe that never came
card.note: Delivery promised by 30 March. 21 days late.

say: She saves the transfer receipt and writes it in her timeline: on 12 March she paid a 50,000 naira deposit, of an agreed 120,000 naira.

card.title: Funmi's wardrobe that never came
card.note: Delivery promised by 30 March. 21 days late.

say: She finds his voice note promising delivery by 30 March. She exports the chat with its media to her Google Drive.
From 30 March to 20 April is 21 days late. She sends him one calm typed message with the dates, and shares the timeline with her estate chairman.

say: Share copies, not originals. And do not delete the chat, even if it is upsetting, until the matter is fully settled.

say: Your safety comes first. Never confront an angry person with a camera. If you are in danger, leave and seek help.
For any court matter or serious dispute, speak to a lawyer, a legal aid service or a trusted community leader first.

say: When you record an elder, ask first and agree who may listen. Choose a quiet time when she is rested. Ask open questions, like: tell me about your wedding day. Record in parts of 10 to 15 minutes with the voice recorder.

panel.heading: Do and don't with an elder's story
left: Ask first, agree who may listen
Quiet place, when she is rested
Record in parts of 10 to 15 minutes
right: Say yes, yes over her words
Rely on WhatsApp for long recordings

say: Listen more than you talk, and let silence bring the memories. Never record someone who is distressed. And if a storyteller changes her mind later, respect it.

say: For example, Rukayat's aunt posts a flood video marked Forwarded many times. Rukayat pauses it and sees shop signs that do not fit their town. Google Lens shows the video is from another country, years earlier.
So run five checks. Who made it? When and where? Does it ask for money or panic? Do trusted sources confirm it? And would sharing hurt someone?

panel.heading: Five checks before forwarding
items: Who made it?
When and where?
Does it ask for money or panic?
Do trusted sources confirm it?
Would sharing hurt someone?

say: To remember. Keep records clear, dated and unedited. Tell stories in three parts. Describe photos in words and type a summary under voice notes, for people who cannot see or hear well.
And if a voice note sounds like a relative asking urgently for money, call back on the number you already have saved.

say: Now practise. Start one real record with a dated timeline. Record one memory, or tell one story in five photos. And describe three photos, then run the five checks on one forwarded item.
